hero.purpose: Landing headline only; Fraunces 300, opsz 144, italic accent phrase.

verdict.purpose: The decision word on the Decision page; italic, tier-colored, largest element.

page-title.purpose: Page headers; founder suffix in italic 300 accent.

memo-heading.purpose: Section heads inside the memo, opsz 72.

headline-figure.purpose: The one serif number that is the headline of its block (channel funnel 21px, axis cell 19px, landing stat 36px, verdict amount 22px).

memo-body.purpose: The memo prose and Ask-this-memo answer; 68ch measure on the page itself, no card.

body.purpose: Default DM Sans UI text and page sub-copy (640px measure).

table.purpose: Ledger cells, nav items, controls; 12.5-13.5px scan layer.

section-kicker.purpose: The one kicker: .section-h h2 with an 18px hairline rule before it.

label.purpose: Column headers, block titles, meter keys, form labels; 0.12em everywhere.

data.purpose: Mono claim ids, inline citations, tier chips, domain chips, formulas; tabular-nums.

shadows.name: ambient-panel-light
shadows.purpose: The only shadow, via var(--shadow), under contained panels in light mode. Dark mode sets --shadow: none.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single state transition token (--ease) for hover, selection, border and background shifts.

motion.name: l-rise
motion.purpose: Landing entrance for h1, sub, stats, CTA. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: Skeleton lines and a busy primary button. Guarded globally by the reduced-motion reset.

motion.name: dilig-spin
motion.purpose: 11px ring while a diligence run is live; reduced-motion sets animation none.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one real action on a view (Submit application, Ask, Export IC memo). Ink text on the light dark-mode accent.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent, #8fb7ea); color: var(--on-accent, #0a1120); border: 1px solid var(--accent, #8fb7ea); border-radius: 4px; padding: 6px 12px; font: 500 12.5px 'DM Sans', -apple-system, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #8fb7ea); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 3px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: .55; cursor: default; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Default action button; transparent with a hairline, accent on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--fg, #edf0f6); border: 1px solid var(--line, #223050); border-radius: 4px; padding: 6px 12px; font: 500 12.5px 'DM Sans', -apple-system, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1), color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: var(--accent, #8fb7ea); color: var(--accent, #8fb7ea); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #8fb7ea); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 3px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Filter / apply / ask input. Panel fill, hairline, no shadow; border carries hover and focus.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" placeholder="e.g. What is the strongest evidence of traction?" />
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: var(--panel, #131e35); color: var(--fg, #edf0f6); border: 1px solid var(--line, #223050); border-radius: 4px; padding: 10px 12px; font: 400 13.5px 'DM Sans', -apple-system, sans-serif; transition: border-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--faint, #8592ab); } .ds-input:hover { border-color: var(--faint, #8592ab); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent, #8fb7ea); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav
components.description: Pipeline rail on the page bg: serif wordmark with accent dot, italic serif tagline, sans items with serif numerals; active item on bg2 with an accent numeral.
components.html:
FirstSignal.
the VC brain for evidence-grounded founder discovery

components.name: Trust-Tier Chip

narrative.overview:
FirstSignal is the screen an associate reads at 11pm before a 9am investment committee. The page is navy ink, not black: a deep blue-black that has a hue the way paper does, with three tonal steps (bg → bg2 → panel) stacked above it and a single hairline doing almost all of the structural work. On that ground the system speaks in two voices. Everything the analyst reads — the page title, the verdict, the memo, evidence quotes, and the one number that is the headline of its block — is set in Fraunces, a soft high-contrast serif with an optical-size axis, ranged from a 300-weight hero to a 46px italic verdict. Everything they scan — tables, labels, controls, meta — is set in DM Sans, quiet and even, at 14px and below. Mono is reserved for claim ids and citations. The intended effect is an elegant institutional site rendered in dark mode: a memo that reads authored, over a data layer that never competes with it.

The surface is flattened. Tables are hairline rows on the page itself with no box; the memo is a document at a 68ch measure, not a card; the verdict is a ruled section; channel yields, landing stats, and the four flow stages are ruled ledger rows. Only genuinely contained things — blocks, the evidence rail, the trace panel, forms, popovers — carry a 1px line border on a panel fill. Dark mode casts no shadow at all; the light fallback allows one soft ambient shadow under panels. One accent, Evidence Blue (a sky blue on the navy), marks citations, current selection, and the primary action, and nothing else. Around it the trust vocabulary — green corroborated, amber single-source, red contradicted, slate self-reported — appears identically on every screen, each hue paired with a text label.

The system rejects consumer-fintech softness, enterprise-legacy chrome, and generic SaaS/AI-dashboard slop. Motion is state-only: one 180ms ease for hover and selection, plus the landing page's single entrance rise, both guarded for reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Dark is canonical; light is the mirrored fallback with identical token names.
Two voices: Fraunces for what is read (titles, verdict, memo, quotes, headline figures), DM Sans for what is scanned (UI, tables, labels), mono for machine identifiers.
Flattened surfaces: hairline rules on the page bg for tables, ledgers and sections; 1px-bordered panels only for contained things; no dark-mode shadow.
Tight radii: 6px blocks, 4px controls, 3px chips. Nothing is a pill.
One kicker system (11px, 0.14em, 18px leading rule) and one label tracking (0.12em) across the product.
One accent (Evidence Blue) for citations, selection, and the primary action; a four-color trust vocabulary that always travels with its text label.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Evidence Blue is the only accent. It appears on citations, current selection, and the one primary action per view; nothing else. Its rarity is what makes a citation legible as a link to proof.

rules.name: The Trust-Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Green/amber/red/slate mean corroborated/single-source/contradicted/self-reported everywhere, without exception. A tier color is never reused for decoration, and it never travels without its text label.

rules.name: The Navy-Not-Black Rule
rules.body: The dark ground is bg (a hued navy ink), never #000 or a neutral gray. Every dark surface — bg, bg2, panel, line, the tier tints — carries the same blue cast so the page reads as one material.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Fraunces sets what the analyst reads: titles, the verdict, the memo and its headings, evidence and quotes, the wordmark, and the single headline figure of a block. DM Sans sets what they scan: body UI, tables, labels, controls. Never set a memo or a title in the sans; never set a table cell, a label, or a control in the serif. Mono is reserved for claim ids and citations.

rules.name: The Light-Display Rule
rules.body: Serif display sizes are set light (300 hero and landing, 400 titles and verdict) with opsz 144. Weight is never the hierarchy device in the serif; size, optical size, italic, and color are.

rules.name: The One-Kicker Rule
rules.body: There is one kicker in the system: the .section-h label, 11px uppercase 0.14em with its 18px leading rule. All other small labels share 0.12em tracking at 600 weight. Do not invent eyebrow variants.

rules.name: The Flat-Terminal Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. Depth is tonal, not cast. If a component seems to need a shadow to separate from its background, the wrong tone is in use: reach for panel over bg, or a hairline rule, instead.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Boxed Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a sequence or a ledger — table rows, channel yields, landing stats, flow stages, the verdict section, the Ask-this-memo block, the latency footer — is separated by 1px line rules on the page bg, not enclosed in a card. A panel border is reserved for things that are genuinely contained: blocks, the evidence rail, the trace, forms, popovers, claim rows.

dos: Do build on the dark tokens first (bg #0a1120, panel #131e35, line #223050, fg #edf0f6) and check the light mirror second; dark is canonical (The Navy-Not-Black Rule).
Do reserve Evidence Blue (#8fb7ea dark / #1d4d8f light) for citations, current selection, the active nav numeral, and the one primary action per view (The One Voice Rule).

Do keep green/amber/red/slate meaning corroborated/single-source/contradicted/self-reported on every screen, and always pair a tier color with its text label (WCAG-AA + colorblind-safe, per PRODUCT.md).

Do set titles, the verdict, memo prose and headings, evidence quotes, the wordmark, and a block's single headline figure in Fraunces; set body UI, tables, labels, and controls in DM Sans; set claim ids and citations in mono (The Two-Voice Rule).
Do keep serif display light: 300 for the hero and landing headings, 400 for page titles and the verdict, opsz 144 at display sizes and 72 for memo headings (The Light-Display Rule).
Do use the one kicker (.section-h h2: 11px, 0.14em, 18px leading rule) for section labels and 10.5px / 0.12em / 600 for every other small label (The One-Kicker Rule).

Do separate sequences and ledgers with 1px line rules on the page bg — tables, channel yields, stats, flow stages, the verdict section — and give a panel border only to things that are contained (The Ruled-Not-Boxed Rule).
Do use the three radii only: 6px blocks, 4px controls, 3px chips.
Do keep --shadow: none in dark mode and the single ambient shadow in light; convey interaction with border and background shifts on the 180ms --ease token.
Do show the three screening axes and the Signal/Coverage split as separate values, never averaged into one number.
Do render gaps and contradictions with weight — the amber gap micro-badge, the red-bordered contradiction spotlight — in the brief's own words, never filled.
Do guard every animation (l-rise, pulse, dilig-spin) with @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce); reduced motion is a PRODUCT.md commitment.
Do apply tabular-nums to every figure regardless of face.
donts: Don't use pure black or neutral gray for a dark surface; every dark tone carries the navy cast.
Don't use pill radii or anything above 6px on a UI element (bars excepted). The old 8/12/20px scale is gone.
Don't put the memo, a table, a stat row, or the verdict inside a card; don't nest cards; don't box a ledger.
Don't set a table cell, label, control, or nav item in Fraunces, and don't set a title, the verdict, or memo prose in DM Sans.
Don't set serif display at 500–600 to make it heavier; use size, italic, optical size, or color instead.
Don't invent a second kicker or eyebrow style; there is one .section-h kicker and one label tracking.
Don't cast shadows in dark mode, use glassmorphism, gradient text, or border-left/border-right color stripes as accents (the 2px trace-signal rail is a quote mark, not an accent).
Don't introduce a second accent hue, reuse a trust-tier color for decoration, or put white text on the dark accent fill (use on-accent).

Don't look like consumer fintech (pastel rounding, playful illustration), enterprise legacy (toolbars, heavy chrome, corporate blues), or generic SaaS/AI dashboards (purple-blue gradients, glass stat cards, big-number KPI grids).
Don't let a wide table scroll the page body; wrap it in .tablewrap.
